subject: spanish
title: Indigenous Heritage
welcome_lead: Indigenous cultures shape Latin American identity. Maya, Aztec, Inca, Mapuche traditions persist alongside Spanish.
meta_desc: Spanish: indigenous heritage in Latin American identity.
final_note: La voz indigena habla — en sus idiomas y en el espanol.

concepts.def: Aztec language, still spoken in Mexico.

walkthroughs.body_html: Mexico recognises 68 indigenous languages. Bolivia made Quechua, Aymara, Guarani official languages alongside Spanish in 2009.
The Virgin of Guadalupe blends Catholic Mary with Aztec mother goddess Tonantzin. Day of the Dead mixes Catholicism with Aztec death cult.
Chocolate, tomate, aguacate (Nahuatl). Cancha, papa, llama (Quechua). The Spanish vocabulary is itself mestiza.
